X-19 Service-to-service communication

Bangla name: সার্ভিস-থেকে-সার্ভিস যোগাযোগ

← 60 · Cross-cutting · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Service-to-service communication. The services call each other synchronously over HTTP with typed clients, and hand off slow work through SQS queues. This file is the reference for who calls whom, with which credentials. Concepts: token forwarding, queue-driven processing, background workers. The architecture document §2.3 describes the same three mechanisms.

2. Trigger and actor

A controller action (user request) or a background worker that needs data or work from another service or an external system.

3. Business flow

Invisible to users. Examples: placing an order makes Booking read event data from Event and later ask Ticketing to create tickets; a worker in Scheduler asks Booking which orders still need a notification.

4. Technical flow

Mechanisms

Tag Mechanism Credential
[HTTP + user token] Typed HttpClient with DelegatedBearerAuthenticationHandler called inside a request The caller's Cognito access token, copied from the AppClaimTypes.AccessToken claim
[HTTP, no token] Same client called from a worker (no HttpContext) none; works only against endpoints without [Authorize] (X-18 category C)
[HTTP, static key] Client with a fixed Authorization header from configuration Notification:Authorization, Serverless:Authorization, gateway/TSP/NBR/OneID credentials
[SQS: Key] SqsPublisher → queue → polling worker AWS static keys AWS:AccessKey/AWS:SecretAccessKey; no token in the message

Most HTTP clients retry transient errors 3 times with exponential back-off (Polly), some with a plain 3-retry policy.

9. Handover notes

  1. Forwarding couples the caller's pool to the callee's policy. A customer request that makes Booking call an Admin-only endpoint would fail; that is why the internal endpoints are anonymous.
  2. Scheduler's IEventClient points at Services:Admin, not Services:Event. The client's paths decide which service answers (S-04).
  3. Services:AppBase is the base URL of IUserClient, which calls user/my-profile with the forwarded token, i.e. the identity API [UNCONFIRMED: Q-01]. Locally it is set to http://localhost:4200/ (scripts/user-secrets.example.json), which is the admin portal, so these calls do not work locally.
  4. Token expiry mid-request: the services do not refresh tokens (architecture §2.3 A).
  5. MassTransit is registered but unused (Appendix A).

Local testability: Full for HTTP and SQS (Floci); external systems are dummies.

Item Detail
Test data and accounts Any; seed data from pwsh ./scripts/Seed-EtpData.ps1

Emulator —
Postman Trigger a cross-service call, e.g. postman/services/etp-admin.postman_collection.json "POST /api/v1/events" (Admin → Event/Booking)
